transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-03-25
Start time: 15:00 PT
Duration: ~55 minutes
Attendees: Samira (Redwood AE), Jorge (Redwood SE), Alex (Summit VP Eng), Priya (Summit Head ML), Derek (Summit SRE), Maya (Procurement)

Summary:
Quick discovery for Dedicated capacity. Summit Bank is leaning toward Dedicated for data isolation and predictable throughput, but wants clarity on burst behaviour, scaling, and security (KMS, SOC2, VPC). They run a mix of embedding and chat/generation workloads and have strict latency SLOs for customer-facing features. Action items and next steps agreed at end.

[00:00] Samira: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, I think we captured most folks, um, quick intro — I'm Samira on the AE side at Redwood, and Jorge's our systems SE who'll go deeper on capacity and networking.
[00:12] Alex: Hey Samira, thanks, Alex here. Quick context, Summit Bank has a bunch of customer-facing features: chat support, document search (embeddings), and some internal summarization pipelines. We're evaluating dedicated GPUs because of PCI/data isolation requirements.
[00:25] Samira: Great, that's exactly what we usually see. Jorge, want to kick off on the capacity model and typical patterns?
[00:30] Jorge: Yeah sure. So Redwood Dedicated is basically reserved GPU pools — you can commit N GPUs, we guarantee that capacity and you get isolation from other tenants. You also get burst credits to handle short spikes, and there's autoscale policy controls. How are you thinking about reserved size?
[00:48] Priya: We're thinking initially around 4 A100-class GPUs, maybe single-digit throughput to start. Our worst-case is about 200 concurrent chat sessions and 2k embedding requests per hour, but those are bursty after marketing pushes. Latency targets are 200-300ms for chat token generation tail p95 ideally.
[01:10] Jorge: Ok, that's helpful. A couple of clarifications: our burst model allows short bursts above committed capacity — it's credit based — but sustained extra load will either queue or you'll need to scale up commit. Also depends on model and token length.
[01:30] Derek: Can you say more about the burst penalties or cost? If we go over, do we get billed at on-demand rates?
[01:36] Samira: Good Q. Bursts are billed separately at higher unit cost; we include example pricing in the quote. For bounded spikes it's usually economical versus permanently sizing up. We'll include a cost comparison for sustained vs burst.
[01:50] Maya: From procurement, we need to know maximum possible overage exposure and SLA credits if performance drops.
[01:56] Jorge: For SLA, our Dedicated contracts include uptime and latency SLOs, and we have automatic fallback policies — you can opt into a lower-cost but compatible model variant as fallback if the primary isn't available.
[02:10] Alex: That fallback raises a concern — we can't send PII to hosted fallbacks. If a fallback routes to any multi-tenant endpoint, that's a non-starter. We need isolation guarantees.
[02:22] Samira: Totally understood. You can configure routing policies so that Dedicated never falls back to hosted; we can do strict isolation, or set fallbacks to only other dedicated variants within your cluster. We'll document that.
[02:35] Priya: Also curious on private deployment options — on-prem vs VPC. Our security team prefers a VPC-based private deployment with customer-managed KMS. How much of the control plane stays with Redwood?
[02:48] Jorge: For Private (VPC) we run a control plane that can be customer-hosted in a private subnet; key management can be customer KMS or HSM. For fully air-gapped on-prem, we have an on-prem package but that takes longer to stand up. For Summit, VPC peering plus KMS integration is usually the sweet spot.
[03:05] Derek: What's the network traffic pattern? We need to know egress, ports, and NAT config.
[03:09] Jorge: We'll share a VPC peering doc — generally TCP on X ports (we'll include specifics), and TLS for control/metrics. Expect some egress to manage updates and telemetry unless you opt out.
[03:22] Alex: Is telemetry optional? We need to keep logs internal sometimes.
[03:26] Samira: You can opt to limit telemetry and keep audit logs forwarded to your SIEM; we support audit log forwarding and can disable PII-level metrics collection.
[03:36] Priya: Ok on models — we plan to run a mix: open weights for embeddings and some smaller LLMs for routing, but vendor models for more complex summarization. Can we pin model versions?
[03:46] Jorge: Yes, model pinning and rollouts are first-class — you can pin versions, do canary or A/B rollouts, and we keep KV cache warm across rollouts to reduce latency.
[03:58] Alex: You mentioned KV cache — is that shared across tenants? Concerned about cross-tenant leakage.
[04:04] Jorge: Good question — in Dedicated the KV cache is per cluster/tenant; we don't cross-share caches. Apologies if the docs we sent earlier were unclear, sometimes the transcriptions say 'K V cash' — but it's per-tenant.
[04:16] Priya: How about quantization? We want to reduce cost with 4-bit quantized models for some workloads. What's supported?
[04:23] Jorge: We support quantized execution paths and can recommend quantization profiles per model and workload. There's a trade-off on quality vs cost; Redwood Optimize will surface recommended profiles.
[04:34] Derek: Latency — you mentioned kernel selection and sequence length optimization. For our chat SLOs, what are typical tail latencies on an A100 for 4k context?
[04:44] Jorge: Depends on model. For a Llama-2-13B style workload with 2k context on A100, p95 token latency is around X-200ms per token; but if you push to 4k it increases. We'll run an actual bench with your prompt set to give concrete numbers.
[05:00] Priya: We'll share sample prompts. Also, do you do prefix caching for embeddings? Sometimes we compute a lot of similar prefixes.
[05:08] Jorge: Yes we have prefix/KV caching; it helps a lot for repeated prompts and system messages. That reduces both cost and latency.
[05:18] Alex: Security/compliance — is Redwood SOC 2 and ISO 27001 certified? Also need audit logs, SAML SSO, RBAC, and KMS.
[05:27] Samira: Redwood has SOC 2 Type II and ISO 27001 in our enterprise package; we integrate with SAML/SSO, support RBAC, and the VPC/private offering supports customer KMS/HSM. We'll share our security pack.
[05:40] Maya: Contractually, Summit needs 7 years of audit trail retention in cold storage for certain records, is that possible?
[05:47] Jorge: We can support long retention as an add-on; we'll map which logs are eligible.
[05:52] Alex: Costing model — show us an example: 4 reserved GPUs, typical monthly tokens, burst profile, and what the cost delta looks like to go 6 GPUs.
[06:02] Samira: We'll include a cost sensitivity table in the pricing. For example, 4 GPUs with moderate burst credits often beats a 6 GPU reserved commit for non-sustained spikes. We'll run the numbers with your QPS.
[06:15] Priya: About rolling updates — if you upgrade kernels or runtime, how disruptive is that? Do we get control over maintenance windows?
[06:22] Jorge: Dedicated clusters have configurable maintenance windows; we do rolling upgrades with minimal disruption and provide pre-upgrade notifications and can perform upgrades during low-traffic windows.
[06:32] Derek: For on-prem, how long to stand up? Our infra team is small — we prefer VPC.
[06:37] Jorge: On-prem typically 8-12 weeks including security review; VPC peering can be days to a couple weeks depending on procurement.
[06:45] Alex: Any examples in financial services?
[06:48] Samira: We have a few banks (non-public customer names in the deck) who've run fraud detection and secure document processing on Dedicated. We'll share redacted case studies.
[06:58] Priya: One more technical — what's the isolation boundary for model weights? Can we bring our own model artifacts and have them only load into our nodes?
[07:06] Jorge: Yes, BYO model artifacts are supported; weights are stored per-tenant and loaded only into your dedicated nodes. We can integrate with your artifact repo and KMS for signing.
[07:18] Alex: Network egress: will any tokens or text be sent to other regions or third parties?
[07:24] Jorge: No, for Dedicated and Private you can restrict egress; control plane updates may reach Redwood endpoints, but we can work to minimize or route via your network.
[07:35] Maya: Procurement question — do you have a standard Master Services Agreement and security addendum?
[07:40] Samira: Yes, we have standard MSAs and can attach a security addendum; I'll loop legal after this call.
[07:46] Priya: On benchmarking — what's the process? We want to run a real workload to validate p95 and cost per request.
[07:53] Jorge: We typically run a 2-4 week pilot with a small reserved footprint and bench it with your prompts; we can provide a benchmark harness and share raw metrics. For summits with regulatory constraints we can run the harness in your VPC.
[08:06] Alex: Time horizon — we're aiming for a pilot in Q2 and production by Q3 if it looks good. Procurement will need vendor risk review and legal.
[08:14] Samira: Sounds reasonable. We'll aim to get the pricing and security docs over this week.
[08:19] Derek: A couple of nitty gritty items: do you expose GPU metrics per instance? We want telemetry for memory pressure and NVLink saturation.
[08:27] Jorge: Yes, per-device telemetry is available and can be forwarded to your monitoring.
[08:32] Priya: For model updates, how do you handle KV cache warm-starts to avoid cold start latency?
[08:38] Jorge: We support cache pre-warming via scheduled jobs and can share tooling to warm KV caches prior to traffic shifts.
[08:45] Samira: Ok let's recap — Samira will send pricing and legal/security pack; Jorge will send VPC/KMS architecture and plan for benching; Summit to share prompt set, QPS profile, and network diagrams.
[08:57] Maya: Procurement, I'll also need payment terms and PO process.
[09:01] Samira: We'll include both monthly and annual commit options in the sheet.
[09:06] Alex: For the benchmark, we want three profiles: peak-chat (short tokens, low latency), bulk-embed (high throughput), and long-context summarization (heavy compute).
[09:14] Jorge: Perfect, we'll parameterize those in the harness.
[09:18] Priya: Quick question — do you have any hard limits on model size for Dedicated on A100s?
[09:24] Jorge: Not hard limits — we support large models; just depends on memory and whether you want to use sharding/partitioning. We'll map model sizes to cluster configs.
[09:34] Alex: Anything we should be aware of in terms of vendor lock-in? We want ability to migrate or run hybrid.
[09:39] Samira: You can export logs, model artifacts, and we support hybrid deployments; the platform is designed to avoid lock-in by supporting standard model formats and offering private deployment options.
[09:50] Derek: OK last security: pen tests — do you allow customer-led penetration tests against your private VPC setup?
[09:56] Jorge: We usually coordinate pen tests; for private deployments we support customer-led pen tests with a review window. We'll include the process in the security docs.
[10:06] Samira: Alright, wrapping up — thanks everyone. We'll follow up on the items discussed.

End recap (auto):
- Pricing and contract options to Samira (includes burst pricing and overage exposure)
- VPC peering/KMS diagram from Jorge
- Benchmark harness + sample script; Summit to share prompts and QPS profile
- Legal/security pack + SLA details

References mentioned in call:
- Redwood Dedicated docs (link shared in chat)
- VPC peering diagram (will be shared)
- Security pack: SOC2, ISO27001, SAML SSO, KMS integration (will share PDF)

Transcript notes: occasional transcription artifacts (e.g., 'K V cash' for KV cache), some speaker labels generic; filled pauses and cross-talk present.
